name: Sumerian City-States & Akkadian Empire
summary: Cradle of urban civilization between the Tigris and Euphrates. Invented cuneiform writing, the potter’s and vehicular wheel, base-60 mathematics (60-minute hour, 360° circle), ziggurats, the Epic of Gilgamesh, and the world’s first empire under Sargon of Akkad.
keyFacts: Cuneiform script (c. 3200 BCE) & Epic of Gilgamesh
Sexagesimal (base-60) mathematics, astronomy, and wheeled transport
Great Ziggurat of Ur & Code of Ur-Nammu (2100 BCE)

name: Old Babylonia, Assyria & Elam
summary: Hammurabi united Mesopotamia and erected his famous basalt stele of 282 laws, while Babylonian mathematicians recorded Plimpton 322 (Pythagorean triples a millennium before Pythagoras) and algebraic tables.
keyFacts: Old Babylonian algebra and Plimpton 322 trigonometric tablet

name: Hittite Empire
summary: Indo-European superpower centered in Anatolia that pioneered early ironworking, three-man war chariots, and international treaty law, rivaling New Kingdom Egypt across Syria and the Levant.
keyFacts: Oldest surviving Indo-European written texts (Hittite cuneiform)
Early meteoric and smelted ironworking & Kadesh Peace Treaty

name: Neo-Assyrian & Neo-Babylonian Empires
summary: The Neo-Assyrian Empire forged the first iron-equipped standing army and Ashurbanipal’s 30,000-tablet Library of Nineveh, followed by the Neo-Babylonian renaissance of glazed-brick Ishtar Gate architecture and predictive mathematical astronomy.
keyFacts: Royal Library of Ashurbanipal at Nineveh (preserving the Epic of Gilgamesh)
Ishtar Gate of Babylon & Chaldean saros-cycle eclipse astronomy
